items.title: Janis Siegel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 2015
items.q: I cite as some of the best examples Fred Hersch, John DiMartino, Alan Broadbent, Alan Pasqua, these are great accompanists.

ctx.x: That’s right. What do you like from a piano accompanist, or don’t like?

I don’t like someone who plays on top of what I’m singing. I mean the accompanist should know the melody and know the lyrics I think. I think that helps set the emotional tone of the tune. An accompanist should play around you and lead you, kind of like a current underneath. And I cite as some of the best examples Fred Hersch, John DiMartino, Alan Broadbent, Alan Pasqua, these are great accompanists. They should challenge you I think, and know how to set you up. A lot of pianists don’t know how to
do that. They’ll set you up in some kind of wrong key, or that’s why they really should know — it has to be someone who loves singers and loves songs.
